title: Carbohydrates — Structure, Classification and Functions
shortDescription: From glucose rings to starch granules: how sugars behave in the body and in food processing.
genZNote: Starch is just glucose holding hands in two different styles. Straight line = amylose, branchy chaos = amylopectin.

sections.heading: Chemical Structure
sections.body: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones (or compounds yielding them on hydrolysis), with the general formula Cx(H2O)y for most. Glucose (aldose) and fructose (ketose) both are C6H12O6 but isomers; in solution they exist mostly as ring (pyranose/furanose) forms with α/β anomers. Glycosidic bonds join units.

table.caption: Carbohydrate classes
rows: Reducing; fructose is the sweetest natural sugar
Fermented by gut bacteria; gas from pulses
Amylose (α-1,4 linear, ~20–30%), amylopectin (α-1,4 with α-1,6 branches)

sections.heading: Functions and Food Behaviour
bullets: Energy: 4 kcal/g; brain and RBCs depend on glucose; protein-sparing effect.
Glycaemic index (GI) ranks foods by blood-glucose rise relative to glucose; low-GI examples include pulses and whole grains.
Gelatinisation: starch granules swell and thicken on heating in water; retrogradation on cooling causes staling.
Maillard browning (reducing sugar + amino group) and caramelisation (sugars alone at high heat) create colour and flavour.
Reducing sugars give positive Benedict's/Fehling's tests; sucrose does not until hydrolysed (inversion).
Lactose intolerance: lactase deficiency → bloating/diarrhoea; hence fermented dairy is tolerated better.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes/ketones and their polymers that serve as the body's main energy source and as functional ingredients (sweeteners, thickeners, fibre).
keyFacts: Sucrose is non-reducing; maltose and lactose are reducing.
Amylose = linear α-1,4; amylopectin = branched with α-1,6.
Cellulose has β-1,4 bonds that humans cannot digest.

highYieldFacts: Invert sugar = glucose + fructose from sucrose hydrolysis.
commonTraps: Do not say fructose is an aldose — it is a ketose.

questions.explanation: Its anomeric carbons are involved in the glycosidic bond.
